title: Machine learning calculator predicts contrast-induced kidney injury in diabetics
summary: Six machine learning models were developed on 3514 diabetic patients from four hospitals; extreme gradient boosting performed best (AUC 0.816 internally and 0.816 externally) and its top 15 predictors defined a brief model (BCPMD) with an online calculator. Per the abstract, BCPMD gave AUC 0.819 internally, and a prospective cohort of 172 patients was used for further validation. Performance is moderate.
ai_technology: XGBoost-derived BCPMD model with SHAP explanation and an online calculator
organization: Sir Run Run Hospital, Nanjing Medical University

evidence.tested: Internal and external validation across four hospitals and validation on a prospective cohort of 172 patients.
evidence.unknown: Results beyond the internal-validation figure were truncated in the abstract; effect of the calculator on outcomes; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts contrast-induced acute kidney injury after PCI in diabetic patients.
